{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01EbT9rC3Yg3VswytYm4aNjM","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Objective Medical Systems, LLC — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-16\n     4→Developer website: https://objectivemedicalsystems.com/\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Objective Medical Systems (OMS) is a small, privately held health IT company headquartered in Houma, Louisiana, founded in 2007–2008 by practicing cardiologists Dr. Vinod Nair, Dr. Peter Fail, and Dr. Richard Abben. The company has approximately 17 employees (per PitchBook) and focuses exclusively on cardiovascular medicine. Their tagline is \"built for cardiologists, by cardiologists.\" Dr. Nair serves as President and Chief Software Architect; Colby LeMaire is CEO. The company was part of the New Orleans BioInnovation Center startup ecosystem, and Dr. Nair was named to the Silicon Bayou 100 list of Louisiana tech innovators.\n     9→\n    10→OMS serves mid-size to large cardiology practices and hospital cardiology service lines. Their named customers include the Cardiovascular Institute of the South (CIS) — the largest single-specialty cardiology practice in Louisiana — Midwest Cardiovascular Institute, and Lane Regional Medical Center. They have a partnership with MedAxiom, described as the nation's leading cardiovascular performance community. The company has no disclosed venture funding, no G2 presence, and almost no independent reviews (one 5-star review on Software Finder from 2016). This is consistent with a very niche vendor serving a small number of specialized customers.\n    11→\n    12→## Product: OMS EHR\n    13→\n    14→CHPL ID: 11751 (OMS EHR Version 6, certified January 8, 2026, Drummond Group ONC-ACB)\n    15→\n    16→### What It Is\n    17→\n    18→OMS EHR is a cardiology-specific electronic health record with an integrated cardiovascular information system (CVIS). It is ONC-certified (HTI-1) with broad criterion coverage: clinical data (a)(1)–(a)(5), (a)(12), (a)(14); transitions of care (b)(1)–(b)(3); patient portal (e)(1); FHIR APIs (g)(7)–(g)(10); clinical quality measures (c)(1)–(c)(3); and public health reporting (f)(7). The SED intended user description is \"Medical/Cardiology.\"\n    19→\n    20→The certified module appears to be the core of a broader product ecosystem that also includes diagnostic reporting, chronic care coordination, AI-powered analytics, and remote patient monitoring — but the EHR is the central certified product.\n    21→\n    22→The system runs on a **Windows/SQL Server on-premises architecture** (Windows 2008 Server R2, SQL Server 2008, .NET 4.7, IIS per the disclosures page). Cloud infrastructure is used for e-prescribing services via ClearDATA.\n    23→\n    24→### Users & Market\n    25→\n    26→**End users:** Cardiologists, cardiology practice staff, diagnostic technicians, and care coordinators. The SED description confirms the target is medical/cardiology users.\n    27→\n    28→**Clinical settings:** Single-specialty cardiology practices ranging from individual hospital departments (Lane Regional Medical Center) to large multi-site groups (Cardiovascular Institute of the South with system-wide deployment). Also serves practices within the MedAxiom network.\n    29→\n    30→**Customer count:** Not publicly disclosed. The named reference customers are CIS, Midwest Cardiovascular Institute, and Lane Regional Medical Center. The extremely thin review footprint (1 review across all platforms) suggests a small installed base, likely dozens of sites rather than hundreds.\n    31→\n    32→**Market position:** Niche cardiology EHR. Appears on \"best of\" lists for cardiology EHR systems (EHR in Practice, FindEMR). Competes in a specialized segment against larger EHR vendors that serve cardiology among other specialties.\n    33→\n    34→### Modules & Functionality\n    35→\n    36→Based on the vendor website, disclosures page, third-party reviews, and press releases, OMS EHR includes:\n    37→\n    38→**Core EHR:**\n    39→- Cardiology-specific charting and documentation\n    40→- Input via traditional typing, e-Ink, handwriting recognition, voice transcription (Nuance integration), and cardiology-specific templates\n    41→- Clinical decision support (drug-drug interactions, drug-allergy checks)\n    42→- Problem lists, medication management, patient demographics\n    43→- Claims to process 6,000+ data points per patient (vendor homepage)\n    44→\n    45→**Cardiovascular Diagnostic Reporting (OMS Diagnostics):**\n    46→- 16 structured reporting modules covering all major cardiovascular diagnostic modalities:\n    47→  - Echocardiography\n    48→  - EKG/ECG\n    49→  - Stress testing\n    50→  - Nuclear/myocardial perfusion imaging\n    51→  - Catheterization lab / invasive cardiology (including 3D heart imaging)\n    52→  - Vascular studies\n    53→  - Holter/ambulatory monitoring\n    54→- This is a core differentiator — the CVIS is tightly integrated with the EHR, not a separate system\n    55→\n    56→**e-Prescribing (CPOE):**\n    57→- Surescripts integration for electronic prescribing with real-time formulary and benefits checking\n    58→- Drug database licensing fee (noted on disclosures page)\n    59→- E-prescribing infrastructure hosted on ClearDATA HIPAA-compliant ACE/ARB), CMS138v6 (tobacco screening), CMS144v6 (heart failure beta-blocker), CMS145v6 (CAD beta-blocker), CMS156v6 (high-risk medications in elderly), CMS164v6 (IVD aspirin), CMS165v6 (hypertension control)\n    63→\n    64→**Transitions of Care & Messaging:**\n    65→- Direct secure messaging via Updox\n    66→- C-CDA generation and receipt (certified for (b)(1)–(b)(3))\n    67→\n    68→**Patient Access:**\n    69→- Patient portal / view-download-transmit (certified for (e)(1))\n    70→- Patient mobile app mentioned on vendor website\n    71→\n    72→**FHIR API Access:**\n    73→- Certified for (g)(7)–(g)(10) — standardized API for patient and population services\n    74→\n    75→**Coding Support:**\n    76→- ICD-9/ICD-10 coding via IMO (Intelligent Medical Objects) — service remote monitoring data:**\n   136→- RPM device readings (blood pressure, heart rate) via C3 platform\n   137→- Chronic care management encounter data\n   138→- Transitional care management data\n   139→\n   140→**Exchange data:**\n   141→- C-CDA documents (sent and received)\n   142→- Direct secure messages (via Updox)\n   143→- FHIR resources (via certified API endpoints)\n   144→\n The company has approximately 17 employees (per PitchBook) and focuses exclusively on cardiovascular medicine. Their tagline is \"built for cardiologists, by cardiologists.\" Dr. Nair serves as President and Chief Software Architect; Colby LeMaire is CEO. The company was part of the New Orleans BioInnovation Center startup ecosystem, and Dr. Nair was named to the Silicon Bayou 100 list of Louisiana tech innovators.\n\nOMS serves mid-size to large cardiology practices and hospital cardiology service lines. Their named customers include the Cardiovascular Institute of the South (CIS) — the largest single-specialty cardiology practice in Louisiana — Midwest Cardiovascular Institute, and Lane Regional Medical Center. They have a partnership with MedAxiom, described as the nation's leading cardiovascular performance community. The company has no disclosed venture funding, no G2 presence, and almost no independent reviews (one 5-star review on Software Finder from 2016). This is consistent with a very niche vendor serving a small number of specialized customers.\n\n## Product: OMS EHR\n\nCHPL ID: 11751 (OMS EHR Version 6, certified January 8, 2026, Drummond Group ONC-ACB)\n\n### What It Is\n\nOMS EHR is a cardiology-specific electronic health record with an integrated cardiovascular information system (CVIS). It is ONC-certified (HTI-1) with broad criterion coverage: clinical data (a)(1)–(a)(5), (a)(12), (a)(14); transitions of care (b)(1)–(b)(3); patient portal (e)(1); FHIR APIs (g)(7)–(g)(10); clinical quality measures (c)(1)–(c)(3); and public health reporting (f)(7). The SED intended user description is \"Medical/Cardiology.\"\n\nThe certified module appears to be the core of a broader product ecosystem that also includes diagnostic reporting, chronic care coordination, AI-powered analytics, and remote patient monitoring — but the EHR is the central certified product.\n\nThe system runs on a **Windows/SQL Server on-premises architecture** (Windows 2008 Server R2, SQL Server 2008, .NET 4.7, IIS per the disclosures page). Cloud infrastructure is used for e-prescribing services via ClearDATA.\n\n### Users & Market\n\n**End users:** Cardiologists, cardiology practice staff, diagnostic technicians, and care coordinators. The SED description confirms the target is medical/cardiology users.\n\n**Clinical settings:** Single-specialty cardiology practices ranging from individual hospital departments (Lane Regional Medical Center) to large multi-site groups (Cardiovascular Institute of the South with system-wide deployment). Also serves practices within the MedAxiom network.\n\n**Customer count:** Not publicly disclosed. The named reference customers are CIS, Midwest Cardiovascular Institute, and Lane Regional Medical Center. The extremely thin review footprint (1 review across all platforms) suggests a small installed base, likely dozens of sites rather than hundreds.\n\n**Market position:** Niche cardiology EHR. Appears on \"best of\" lists for cardiology EHR systems (EHR in Practice, FindEMR). Competes in a specialized segment against larger EHR vendors that serve cardiology among other specialties.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nBased on the vendor website, disclosures page, third-party reviews, and press releases, OMS EHR includes:\n\n**Core EHR:**\n- Cardiology-specific charting and documentation\n- Input via traditional typing, e-Ink, handwriting recognition, voice transcription (Nuance integration), and cardiology-specific templates\n- Clinical decision support (drug-drug interactions, drug-allergy checks)\n- Problem lists, medication management, patient demographics\n- Claims to process 6,000+ data points per patient (vendor homepage)\n\n**Cardiovascular Diagnostic Reporting (OMS Diagnostics):**\n- 16 structured reporting modules covering all major cardiovascular diagnostic modalities:\n  - Echocardiography\n  - EKG/ECG\n  - Stress testing\n  - Nuclear/myocardial perfusion imaging\n  - Catheterization lab / invasive cardiology (including 3D heart imaging)\n  - Vascular studies\n  - Holter/ambulatory monitoring\n- This is a core differentiator — the CVIS is tightly integrated with the EHR, not a separate system\n\n**e-Prescribing (CPOE):**\n- Surescripts integration for electronic prescribing with real-time formulary and benefits checking\n- Drug database licensing fee (noted on disclosures page)\n- E-prescribing infrastructure hosted on ClearDATA HIPAA-compliant cloud\n\n**Clinical Quality Measures:**\n- Certified on 14 CQMs, heavily cardiology-relevant: CMS22v6 (preventive care/blood pressure screening), CMS50v6 (closing referral loop), CMS65v7 (hypertension improvement), CMS68v7 (documentation of current meds), CMS69v6 (BMI screening), CMS122v6 (diabetes HbA1c control), CMS134v6 (diabetes nephropathy), CMS135v6 (heart failure ACE/ARB), CMS138v6 (tobacco screening), CMS144v6 (heart failure beta-blocker), CMS145v6 (CAD beta-blocker), CMS156v6 (high-risk medications in elderly), CMS164v6 (IVD aspirin), CMS165v6 (hypertension control)\n\n**Transitions of Care & Messaging:**\n- Direct secure messaging via Updox\n- C-CDA generation and receipt (certified for (b)(1)–(b)(3))\n\n**Patient Access:**\n- Patient portal / view-download-transmit (certified for (e)(1))\n- Patient mobile app mentioned on vendor website\n\n**FHIR API Access:**\n- Certified for (g)(7)–(g)(10) — standardized API for patient and population services\n\n**Coding Support:**\n- ICD-9/ICD-10 coding via IMO (Intelligent Medical Objects) — service fee\n- CPT coding support\n\n**OMS C3 (Chronic Care Coordinator):**\n- Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) for chronic cardiovascular conditions\n- Chronic Care Management (CCM) workflows\n- Transitional Care Management (TCM)\n- Bluetooth-enabled device integration for blood pressure, heart rate monitoring\n- Used by Midwest Cardiovascular Institute for their \"Cardio@Home\" program (May 2025)\n- Launched in 2017 per BusinessWire press release\n\n**AI-Powered Features (introduced 2024):**\n- **AskOMS** — AI clinical assistant\n- **Diagnosis Detection** — Named entity recognition to identify diagnoses from assessment/plan text; supports coding enhancement\n- **Clinical Trial Identification** — Patient-to-trial matching\n- **Patient No-Show Prediction** — Predictive analytics for scheduling\n\n**Operational Tools:**\n- **Trace Analytics / Cardiolytica** — Population health analytics (launched 2018)\n- **Patient Recall** — Automated patient outreach and recall\n- **Smart Scan** — Automated document filing into the EHR\n- **Patient Risk Assessment** — Framingham Risk Scorecard\n\n**Revenue Cycle:**\n- Revenue cycle management is mentioned on the vendor homepage as part of the product's capabilities, though detail is limited\n\n**Lab Integration:**\n- Lab results integration is referenced in the context of clinical decision support and diagnostic workflows\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on the modules and features described above, OMS EHR stores and manages:\n\n**Clinical data (directly evidenced):**\n- Patient demographics and clinical history\n- Cardiovascular diagnostic reports across all modalities (echo, EKG, stress, nuclear, cath lab, vascular, Holter) — this is the product's core strength, with 16 structured reporting modules\n- Problem lists, diagnoses, conditions\n- Medications and prescriptions (Surescripts e-prescribing)\n- Allergies and drug interactions\n- Lab results\n- Vital signs (including remote monitoring data — blood pressure, heart rate via Bluetooth devices)\n- Clinical notes and assessments (with AI-assisted diagnosis detection)\n- Immunizations (implied by (a)(14) certification)\n- Care plans\n- Procedures and surgical data (cath lab reporting implies procedural data)\n\n**Documents and imaging:**\n- Scanned documents (Smart Scan auto-filing)\n- Diagnostic images associated with cardiovascular studies\n- Binary/media content (implied by CVIS integration)\n\n**Administrative and operational data:**\n- Scheduling and appointments (patient no-show prediction implies appointment data)\n- Patient recall records\n- Clinical quality measure data and reporting\n- Revenue cycle / billing data (mentioned but with limited detail — unclear how deep billing functionality goes vs. external billing integration)\n- Referral tracking (CMS50 closing the referral loop implies referral data)\n- Audit events (certified for (d)(2)–(d)(3))\n\n**Patient-generated and remote monitoring data:**\n- RPM device readings (blood pressure, heart rate) via C3 platform\n- Chronic care management encounter data\n- Transitional care management data\n\n**Exchange data:**\n- C-CDA documents (sent and received)\n- Direct secure messages (via Updox)\n- FHIR resources (via certified API endpoints)\n\n**What's unclear:**\n- The depth of billing/revenue cycle functionality — whether OMS handles full claims management, charge capture, and ERA/EOB processing, or whether billing is primarily handled by external practice management systems. The disclosures page mentions CPT coding and ICD coding fees but doesn't describe claims submission.\n- Whether there is a separate practice management system or if PM functionality is embedded in the EHR\n- The extent of patient portal data (messaging, appointment requests, bill pay, etc.)\n- Whether clinical trial matching data and AI analytics data are stored within the EHR database or in separate systems\n\n---\n","numLines":152,"startLine":1,"totalLines":152}}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01YGsrk7p5ycmrXqtptRUvz9","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01M94d5KkLfxoDycZNBAe7s4","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/objective-medical-systems-llc--oms-ehr/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# Objective Medical Systems, LLC — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-16\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://objectivemedicalsystems.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/EHI-Export-Data-Format.pdf\n- CHPL ID: 11751\n- Product: OMS EHR Version 6, certified 2026-01-08\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\nThe registered URL is a direct PDF download hosted on WordPress (Cloudflare CDN).\n\n```bash\n# Probe headers — confirmed direct PDF download\ncurl -sI -L \"https://objectivemedicalsystems.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/EHI-Export-Data-Format.pdf\" \\\n  -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n# → HTTP/2 200, content-type: application/pdf, content-length: 133402\n\n# Download the PDF\ncurl -sL \"https://objectivemedicalsystems.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/EHI-Export-Data-Format.pdf\" \\\n  -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' \\\n  -o downloads/EHI-Export-Data-Format.pdf\n\n# Verified: file(1) confirms \"PDF document, version 1.7, 2 page(s)\"\n```\n\nThe disclosures page at https://objectivemedicalsystems.com/disclosures/ links to an HTML version at https://objectivemedicalsystems.com/ehi-export-data-format/ — but this URL serves the identical PDF file (same 133,402 bytes). No additional EHI export documentation was found on the disclosures page or elsewhere on the site.\n\nThe PDF was authored by Anand Aravind using Microsoft Word for Microsoft 365, created 2023-11-16 and never modified since.\n\nNo embedded URLs, attachments, or links to additional documents were found in the PDF.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe entire EHI export documentation is a 2-page PDF:\n\n- **Page 1**: Title page — \"§170.315(b)(10) Electronic Health Information Export Data Format\" with company logo and address.\n- **Page 2**: A single table listing 9 \"functionalities\" and their export file format:\n\n| Function | Doc Type |\n|---|---|\n| CCDA | XML, HTML |\n| Notes | HTML |\n| C3 Notes | HTML |\n| Labs | XML, HTML |\n| Labs Scanned | PDF |\n| Diagnostics | Discrete fields, PDF |\n| Scanned documents | PDF |\n| Smart Forms | HTML |\n| Messages | Discrete fields |\n\nA note states: \"Documents sourced from outside will be exported in the same format it was received.\"\n\nThat is the entirety of the documentation. There is no data dictionary, no field-level definitions, no schema, no sample data, no export instructions, no API specification, and no description of how the export is initiated or delivered.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nOMS EHR is a cardiology-specific EHR with an integrated cardiovascular information system (CVIS) that stores an unusually rich and deep set of specialty clinical data: 16 structured diagnostic reporting modules covering echocardiography, EKG, stress testing, nuclear imaging, catheterization lab, vascular studies, and Holter monitoring, plus chronic care coordination (C3), remote patient monitoring data, AI-assisted diagnosis detection, and revenue cycle data.\n\nThe export documentation lists 9 high-level categories. Mapping these against what the product actually stores:\n\n**Likely covered (at least partially):**\n- **Clinical notes** → \"Notes\" (HTML) and \"C3 Notes\" (HTML) likely cover progress notes and chronic care coordination notes\n- **CCDA summary data** → \"CCDA\" (XML, HTML) likely covers demographics, problems, medications, allergies, immunizations, vitals — the standard clinical summary\n- **Lab results** → \"Labs\" (XML, HTML) and \"Labs Scanned\" (PDF)\n- **Cardiovascular diagnostics** → \"Diagnostics\" (Discrete fields, PDF) — this is the product's core differentiator, but \"discrete fields\" is undefined\n- **Forms** → \"Smart Forms\" (HTML) covers custom form data\n- **Messages** → \"Messages\" (Discrete fields) covers internal messaging\n- **Scanned/external documents** → \"Scanned documents\" (PDF) and the note about external documents\n\n**Not mentioned or clearly missing:**\n- **Patient demographics** — not listed as a separate export category (may be in CCDA but unclear if full demographic record is exported)\n- **Medications and prescriptions** — not listed separately; Surescripts e-prescribing data may only appear in CCDA summary\n- **Billing and revenue cycle data** — completely absent from the export documentation. OMS mentions revenue cycle management on their homepage and uses CPT/ICD coding; none of this appears in the export.\n- **Remote patient monitoring data** — the C3 platform captures blood pressure and heart rate readings from Bluetooth devices. \"C3 Notes\" may cover coordinator notes but RPM device readings/time-series data are not addressed.\n- **Referral data** — OMS is certified for CMS50 (closing the referral loop) but referrals are not mentioned in the export.\n- **Care plans and goals** — not mentioned.\n- **Immunizations** — not mentioned separately (may be in CCDA).\n- **Procedures and surgical data** — catheterization lab data implies procedural records, but procedures are not mentioned as an export category.\n- **Insurance/coverage information** — not mentioned.\n- **Patient portal data** — not mentioned.\n\nThe fundamental issue is that the CCDA export (which follows the C-CDA standard) covers only the USCDI/US Core clinical summary subset. The remaining categories are document-oriented exports (HTML, PDF) that capture rendered content but may not preserve the underlying discrete data in a computably useful form. The \"Diagnostics\" and \"Messages\" categories mention \"discrete fields\" but provide zero detail about what those fields are.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses a mix of formats:\n- **C-CDA XML/HTML** for clinical summaries — this is a recognized standard but covers only the (g)(10) clinical data subset\n- **HTML** for notes, C3 notes, and smart forms — rendered documents, not structured data\n- **PDF** for scanned documents and lab scans — essentially image exports\n- **\"Discrete fields\"** for diagnostics and messages — completely undefined; no schema, no field listing, no format specification\n\nThe term \"discrete fields\" is the most intriguing and the least documented. For a cardiology CVIS that stores structured echocardiography measurements, catheterization data, and other numeric/coded diagnostic data, \"discrete fields\" could represent genuinely valuable structured export — but without any specification of what fields, what format, or what structure, it is impossible to assess.\n\nThere is no mention of FHIR, NDJSON, CSV, SQL dump, or any bulk data format. The export appears to be a document-level export (one document per category per patient) rather than a database-level export.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThis is among the most minimal EHI export documentation possible. The entire substantive content fits in a single table with 9 rows and 2 columns. There is:\n\n- **No data dictionary** — not a single field name is defined\n- **No schema or format specification** — \"discrete fields\" is not defined\n- **No sample data or examples**\n- **No export instructions** — how does a user initiate an export? Is it per-patient? Bulk?\n- **No field-level definitions** — for any category\n- **No value sets or coded field documentation**\n- **No relationship documentation** — how do the exported pieces relate to each other?\n- **No worked examples**\n\nA developer could not implement an import of this data based on this documentation. A patient or provider receiving this export would have no specification to interpret the \"discrete fields\" exports.\n\nThe document was created in November 2023 and has not been updated since, despite the product being certified in January 2026. The certification is very recent (5 weeks ago), which may partially explain the sparse documentation, though the PDF predates the certification by over 2 years.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\nThe documentation provides only category-level granularity (9 categories). There is no field-level documentation whatsoever. This is essentially a list of export file types, not a data dictionary or format specification.\n\n**What's critically missing for a cardiology CVIS:**\n- The 16 structured diagnostic reporting modules (echo, EKG, stress, nuclear, cath lab, vascular, Holter) are collapsed into a single \"Diagnostics\" row with \"Discrete fields, PDF\" — no information about what discrete fields are exported for any modality\n- Remote patient monitoring time-series data (blood pressure, heart rate readings) from the C3/Cardio@Home platform — not addressed\n- Billing/claims data — absent entirely\n- The claim of processing \"6,000+ data points per patient\" on the vendor homepage vs. 9 export categories with no field documentation is a stark contrast\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL: https://objectivemedicalsystems.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/EHI-Export-Data-Format.pdf (no redirect)\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none (Cloudflare present but did not block curl)\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n\nNone. The URL worked perfectly and the download was straightforward. The obstacle is the content itself — there is almost nothing to download. The disclosures page was checked for additional documentation links but none were found beyond the same PDF.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":195,"cache_read_input_tokens":64842,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":195},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"d92886bf-a994-433a-8f0e-4ba24c1b3986","uuid":"733e812c-7b3e-4e5c-9f68-f33454a3e703"}

The export appears to be a document-level export (one document per category per patient) rather than a database-level export.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThis is among the most minimal EHI export documentation possible. The entire substantive content fits in a single table with 9 rows and 2 columns. There is:\n\n- **No data dictionary** — not a single field name is defined\n- **No schema or format specification** — \"discrete fields\" is not defined\n- **No sample data or examples**\n- **No export instructions** — how does a user initiate an export? Is it per-patient? Bulk?\n- **No field-level definitions** — for any category\n- **No value sets or coded field documentation**\n- **No relationship documentation** — how do the exported pieces relate to each other?\n- **No worked examples**\n\nA developer could not implement an import of this data based on this documentation. A patient or provider receiving this export would have no specification to interpret the \"discrete fields\" exports.\n\nThe document was created in November 2023 and has not been updated since, despite the product being certified in January 2026. The certification is very recent (5 weeks ago), which may partially explain the sparse documentation, though the PDF predates the certification by over 2 years.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\nThe documentation provides only category-level granularity (9 categories). There is no field-level documentation whatsoever. This is essentially a list of export file types, not a data dictionary or format specification.\n\n**What's critically missing for a cardiology CVIS:**\n- The 16 structured diagnostic reporting modules (echo, EKG, stress, nuclear, cath lab, vascular, Holter) are collapsed into a single \"Diagnostics\" row with \"Discrete fields, PDF\" — no information about what discrete fields are exported for any modality\n- Remote patient monitoring time-series data (blood pressure, heart rate readings) from the C3/Cardio@Home platform — not addressed\n- Billing/claims data — absent entirely\n- The claim of processing \"6,000+ data points per patient\" on the vendor homepage vs. 9 export categories with no field documentation is a stark contrast\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL: https://objectivemedicalsystems.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/EHI-Export-Data-Format.pdf (no redirect)\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none (Cloudflare present but did not block curl)\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n\nNone. The URL worked perfectly and the download was straightforward. The obstacle is the content itself — there is almost nothing to download.
